svg.title: Two valid probability tables have variance three
svg.desc: A variable takes zero and four, with probability p at four. Its mean is four p and second moment sixteen p. The variance curve sixteen p times one minus p is drawn on the complete probability domain zero through one. A horizontal target line at variance three intersects at p one quarter and three quarters. The corresponding tables have probabilities three quarters and one quarter at zero and four, or one quarter and three quarters. Their means are one and three, and both variances equal three. Both roots are admissible from the variance alone; the additional mean below two condition selects p one quarter.
